jp: 当店[とうてん]には、和食[わしょく]のコースが三[みっ]つ{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Our restaurant has three Japanese-style courses.
why: A shop staff member says a thing exists in formal speech: ございます replaces あります; おる and いらっしゃる are for people.

jp: お会計[かいけい]は全部[ぜんぶ]で三千五百円[さんぜんごひゃくえん]{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Your total comes to three thousand five hundred yen.
why: Noun + です becomes noun + でございます in formal speech; でいらっしゃる and でおる are for people.

jp: 申[もう]し訳[わけ]ございませんが、本日[ほんじつ]そのお品[しな]は在庫[ざいこ]が{ございません|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: I am very sorry, but that item is out of stock today.
why: Formal negative of ある for a thing is ございません; おりません is for people, and ございます would reverse the meaning.

jp: お飲[の]み物[もの]はコーヒーと紅茶[こうちゃ]が{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}が、いかがなさいますか。
en: We have coffee and tea; which would you like?
why: Drinks are things, so the formal existence verb ございます is used; the others are for living beings.

jp: お客様[きゃくさま]、両替[りょうがえ]の機械[きかい]はあちらに{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Sir, the currency exchange machine is over there.
why: A machine is a thing, so ございます; おる and いらっしゃる are for people and animals.

jp: こちらがお釣[つ]りの五百円[ごひゃくえん]{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Here is your change, five hundred yen.
why: This identifies the change (A は B です), so the copula form でございます is needed.

jp: お客様[きゃくさま]、お探[さが]しの靴[くつ]は、こちらの棚[たな]に{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Sir, the shoes you are looking for are on this shelf.
why: Shoes are things in a location, so ございます; でございます is for equating two nouns.

jp: お支払[しはら]いは現金[げんきん]のみ{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
why: A statement about what the payment is takes noun + でございます; ございます alone cannot follow a noun here.

jp: お電話[でんわ]ありがとうございます。山田[やまだ]書店[しょてん]{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Thank you for calling. This is Yamada Bookshop.
why: Answering the phone, staff name their own shop with noun + でございます; でいらっしゃる would honour themselves.

jp: こちらのワインは、フランス産[さん]{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
why: Identifying a thing as a noun uses でございます; でいらっしゃる and でおる are for people.

jp: 本日[ほんじつ]のおすすめは、鯛[たい]のお造[つく]り{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Today's recommendation is sliced sea bream sashimi.
why: A dish named as the recommendation is an A = B statement, so でございます.

jp: レジ袋[ぶくろ]は有料[ゆうりょう]{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Plastic shopping bags are charged for.
why: Na-adjective or noun + です becomes でございます; ございます alone would say that bags exist.

jp: お子様[こさま]用[よう]の椅子[いす]も{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: We also have chairs for children.
why: Chairs are things that exist, so ございます is the formal verb; おる and いらっしゃる are for living beings.

jp: ただいま、全[すべ]ての商品[しょうひん]がセール中[ちゅう]{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: All our products are on sale at the moment.
why: A state described with a noun (セール中) takes でございます; the present tense matches ただいま.

jp: ご予算[よさん]に合[あ]うお品[しな]が、他[ほか]にも{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}が、ご覧[らん]になりますか。
en: We have other items within your budget; would you like to see them?
why: Items exist (a thing), so ございます; ございません would contradict the offer to show them.

jp: 当店[とうてん]は、創業[そうぎょう]百年[ひゃくねん]の老舗[しにせ]{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Our shop is a long-established store, founded one hundred years ago.
why: Describing what the shop is uses noun + でございます; でいらっしゃる is for people.

jp: あいにく、当店[とうてん]に駐車場[ちゅうしゃじょう]は{ございません|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: I'm afraid our shop has no parking lot.
why: A parking lot is a thing and it is absent: ございません; ございます would say the opposite.

jp: お待[ま]たせしました。ご注文[ちゅうもん]のカレー{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Sorry to keep you waiting. Here is the curry you ordered.
why: Serving a dish and naming it is A = B, so noun + でございます.

jp: お取[と]り置[お]きの商品[しょうひん]は、レジの奥[おく]に{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: The item we are holding for you is behind the register.
why: A location with に and a thing takes ございます; おる and いらっしゃる are for living beings.
